## What Was Implemented
"kitty": a stdlib-only Python 3.9.6 command-line tool (`python3 -m kitty <command>`) that tracks shared trip costs in `kitty.json` in the current directory and prints JSON reports (members, expenses with equal/among/exact/shares/percent splits and foreign currencies, payments, rates, balances, settle, history, category report, CSV export). Built in 7 tasks on branch `build` in /private/tmp/tmp12kvlzsp/pete/projects/kitty. The owner is not a programmer; their friend Sam will script against the JSON output.

## Requirements / Plan
- Spec (binding authority): /private/tmp/tmp12kvlzsp/pete/projects/kitty/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-17-kitty-design.md
- Plan: /private/tmp/tmp12kvlzsp/pete/projects/kitty/docs/superpowers/plans/2026-11-17-kitty.md
- Progress ledger with rulings, parked and deferred-minor findings from per-task reviews (triage which must be fixed before merge): /private/tmp/tmp12kvlzsp/pete/projects/kitty/.superpowers/sdd/2026-11-17-kitty/progress.md

## Git Range to Review
**Base:** c832567
**Head:** a50abc9
The full branch diff (commit list, stat, diff with context) is in one file — read it instead of running git diff: /private/tmp/tmp12kvlzsp/pete/projects/kitty/.superpowers/sdd/2026-11-17-kitty/review-c832567..a50abc9.diff

## The spec is a vision document
The spec says what the software must do. It does not enumerate every input, environment, or condition the software will meet. For behavior the spec is silent on, judge by what a reasonable person using this software would expect: a reasonable person's expectation is a requirement, and a spec's silence is not permission. Grade such findings by their effect on that person, not by whether the spec mentions the trigger.

## Declined to judge
Before your verdict, list every behavior you considered and set aside as outside the plan or spec, one line each, with the reason. An empty list means you set nothing aside.

## Read-Only Review
Read-only on this checkout: do not mutate the working tree, the index, HEAD, or branch state. If you run the tool or tests to probe behaviour, do it from a fresh temp dir you create (`mktemp -d`; check it succeeded) with `PYTHONPATH=/private/tmp/tmp12kvlzsp/pete/projects/kitty` — never run kitty commands in the project folder or its parent directories. Running `python3 -m unittest discover tests` from the project root is fine (tests use temp dirs).

## You Do Not Dispatch Subagents
Do all of this review yourself; review in passes if needed.

## What to Check
Plan alignment (matches spec; deviations justified?; all functionality present), code quality (separation, error handling, DRY, edge cases), architecture, security, testing (real behaviour, edge cases, integration tests), production readiness (docs/README, no obvious bugs). In particular probe: every refusal exits 1 with one `error:` line, no traceback, `kitty.json` byte-for-byte unchanged; Sam's exact JSON examples; cent rounding rules; hand-edited/corrupt kitty.json that passes the top-level key check but has malformed records.

## Calibration
Categorize by actual severity; acknowledge strengths. Flag deviations from the plan and issues with the plan itself.

## Output Format
### Strengths
### Issues
#### Critical (Must Fix)
#### Important (Should Fix)
#### Minor (Nice to Have)
(each: file:line, what's wrong, why it matters, how to fix)
### Triage of ledger deferred/parked items (fix before merge? yes/no each)
### Declined to judge
### Recommendations
### Assessment
**Ready to merge?** [Yes | No | With fixes]
**Reasoning:** [1-2 sentences]

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

A group of friends on a trip need to record who paid for what, so that at

- Track members, expenses (with flexible splits and foreign currencies),
  payments between members, and exchange rates.
- Report balances, a settlement plan, per-person history, a per-category
  spending report, and a CSV export.
- Exact money math: shares of an expense always add up to it to the cent.

- No GUI, no web, no multi-user sync, no editing of an existing expense
  (remove and re-add instead), no automatic exchange-rate lookup.

## Anti-goals (would be a failure even if it "works")

- Needs anything installed beyond the Mac's Python 3.9.6.
- A refused command changes `kitty.json` in any way, or a crash leaves it
  half-written.
- A Python traceback shown to the user for bad input.
- Balances that drift by a cent, or shares that don't sum to the expense.
- Past expenses silently changing when the group or a rate changes.

- Run as `python3 -m kitty <command> ...` from the folder that contains the
  `kitty` package. Python 3.9.6, standard library only (so no `match`, no
  `X | Y` type unions at runtime, `date.fromisoformat` is limited, etc.).
- State lives in `kitty.json` in the **current working directory**.

  stderr, nothing on stdout, exit status 1, `kitty.json` byte-for-byte
  unchanged. This includes command-line usage mistakes (unknown command,
  missing argument, unknown option) — argparse's default exit status 2 must
  be overridden to 1 with the same `error:` format.

## Approaches considered

1. **Plain Python package, stdlib only, JSON file state** — chosen.
   `decimal` for money, `json`, `csv`, `argparse`. Matches every constraint.
2. **SQLite database for state** — rejected: Sam asked for `kitty.json`, and
   a plain JSON file is easier for his scripts.
3. **Third-party libraries (e.g. click, a money library) or another
   language** — rejected: violates "nothing to install" and
   `python3 -m kitty`.

The owner agreed to approach 1.

(`", "` and `": "`), on one line, as in the examples. Money is always a
string with exactly two decimals. Money is in the main (base) currency,
except an expense's own `amount`. Object key order is significant and is
given below.

| Command | Prints on success |

| `init CUR` | nothing |
| `member add NAME` / `member remove NAME` | nothing |
| `member list` | `["Alice", "Bob"]` — join order |
| `expense add PAYER AMOUNT DESCRIPTION [opts]` | the new ID, e.g. `1` |
| `expense list` | list of expense objects, by ID |
| `expense remove ID` | nothing |
| `payment add FROM TO AMOUNT [--currency C] [--date D]` | nothing |
| `rate set CUR RATE` | nothing |
| `balances` | object, members in join order |
| `settle` | list of payments, in the order computed |
| `history NAME` | list of entries |
| `report` | object of objects |
| `export FILE` | nothing (writes the CSV) |

Examples (from Sam):

- `expense list`: `[{"id": 1, "date": "2026-07-14", "payer": "Alice", "description": "Dinner", "amount": "45.00", "currency": "USD", "base_amount": "41.40", "category": "food", "shares": {"Alice": "20.70", "Bob": "20.70"}}]`
- `balances`: `{"Alice": "20.70", "Bob": "-20.70"}`
- `settle`: `[{"from": "Bob", "to": "Alice", "amount": "20.70"}]`
- `history Bob`: `[{"date": "2026-07-14", "description": "Dinner", "change": "-20.70", "balance": "-20.70"}]`
- `report`: `{"food": {"Alice": "20.70", "Bob": "20.70"}}`

Empty results print `[]` or `{}`.

### Kitty and state
- `init CUR` creates `kitty.json` with CUR as the main currency. Refused if
  `kitty.json` already exists. Every other command is refused if it doesn't.
- Anything that changes state is fully validated first; the file is saved
  only on success, by writing a temp file in the same folder and
  `os.replace`-ing it over `kitty.json`.

### Members
- Names are case-insensitive for matching everywhere (in every command and
  option), but always displayed as first added. Adding a name that matches
  an existing one case-insensitively is refused.
- Names may not contain `,` or `=`. (Builder's call: also refuse empty or
  all-whitespace names; strip surrounding whitespace.)
- `member remove` is refused if the person appears in any expense (as payer
  or in its shares) or any payment (as sender or receiver). Otherwise it
  succeeds. Unknown name is refused.

### Expenses
- PAYER must be a member. The payer need not be among the people sharing.
- "Everyone" (no split option) means the members at the moment the expense
  is added; the computed shares are stored with the expense and never
  recomputed. Later joiners are not included in earlier expenses.
- At most one of `--among`, `--exact`, `--shares`, `--percent`.
- `--among A,B`: equal split among those named.
- `--exact A=30,B=20`: amounts in the expense's own currency; must add up

  default is today's local date.

  `expense remove` of an unknown ID is refused.

- AMOUNT (expenses, payments, `--exact` values) must be a positive number
  with at most two decimals. `12.345` is refused, not rounded. Zero,
  negative, and non-numbers are refused.

### Currency and rates
- `rate set USD 0.92`: one USD = 0.92 main currency. Rate must be a
  positive number. Setting a rate for the main currency is refused.
- An expense or payment is converted with the rate in force when it is
  added; that rate is frozen with it. Later `rate set` affects only things
  added afterwards.
- `base_amount = amount × rate`, rounded to the cent with halves always
  going up (0.125 → 0.13).

### Splitting and cents
- Each person's exact part of `base_amount` is computed, rounded **down** to
  the cent, then the leftover cents go out one each, in order, until none
  remain. Order is the order typed in the option, or join order for
  "everyone".

  down, leftover cents in listed order).

### Payments
- FROM and TO must be members and must differ. Same amount, currency, date
  rules as expenses.

### Balances
- balance = (sum of `base_amount` of expenses they paid) − (sum of their
  shares) + (payments they sent) − (payments they received), all in base.
  Positive = owed money, negative = owes. Every member listed in join
  order; zero shows as `"0.00"`.

### Settle
- Repeatedly take the person who owes the most and the person owed the
  most; the payment is whatever amount evens out one of them
  (min of the two magnitudes). Ties for "most" are broken alphabetically,
  ignoring case. Payments listed in the order worked out. Nothing to settle
  → `[]`.

### Errors
- Any refusal leaves `kitty.json` exactly as it was, prints
  `error: <message>` to stderr, exits 1.

- **Description** may be several words without quotes
  (`expense add Alice 45 Dinner at Luigi's`); words are joined with single
  spaces. Options may come before or after it. Empty description refused.

  proportional to their exact amount, then the same round-down/leftover
  rule applies. So shares always sum to `base_amount`; for main-currency
  expenses this reproduces the exact amounts.
- **Order of `shares`** in `expense list` is the split order: the order
  typed in the option, or join order for "everyone". It is stored that way.
- **Zero shares:** everyone named in a split (or everyone, for the default)
  is in the expense, even if their rounded share is `0.00` (e.g. 0.01 among
  three). They appear in `shares`, count as "in" the expense for
  `member remove`, get a `history` entry, and appear in `report` for that
  category.

  be exactly three letters A–Z. `--currency` equal to the main currency is
  allowed (rate 1).

  `inf`. Rates, `--shares` and `--percent` values are positive decimals of
  any precision. `--exact` values follow the amount rule.

  the order things were added (a single global sequence across expenses
  and payments). Running `balance` after each entry; the last equals
  `balances`. Unknown name refused.

  category, only people with a share in it, in join order.

  sequence counter, and the next expense ID), error message wording.

  the cent-rounding cases, and the "file unchanged on refusal" guarantee.

# kitty

Keeps track of shared trip costs: who paid, who owes whom, and how to settle up.
It needs nothing installed except Python 3. Run it from the folder that contains
the `kitty` folder (or set `PYTHONPATH` to that folder). The data lives in a file
called `kitty.json` in the folder you run it from.

Every command starts with `python3 -m kitty`. If something is wrong you get one
line starting with `error:` and nothing is changed.

| What you want | Example |
|---|---|
| Start a new kitty (main currency) | `python3 -m kitty init EUR` |
| Add a person | `python3 -m kitty member add Alice` |
| Remove a person (only if unused) | `python3 -m kitty member remove Alice` |
| List people | `python3 -m kitty member list` |
| Set an exchange rate (1 USD = 0.92 EUR) | `python3 -m kitty rate set USD 0.92` |
| Add an expense (split among everyone) | `python3 -m kitty expense add Alice 45 Dinner --currency USD --date 2026-07-14 --category food` |
| Split among some people | `python3 -m kitty expense add Alice 30 Taxi --among Alice,Bob` |
| Split by exact amounts | `python3 -m kitty expense add Alice 50 Hotel --exact Alice=30,Bob=20` |
| Split by shares | `python3 -m kitty expense add Alice 60 Food --shares Alice=2,Bob=1` |
| Split by percent | `python3 -m kitty expense add Alice 100 Tickets --percent Alice=60,Bob=40` |
| List expenses | `python3 -m kitty expense list` |
| Remove an expense | `python3 -m kitty expense remove 1` |
| Record a payback | `python3 -m kitty payment add Bob Alice 20.70` |
| Who is owed / owes what | `python3 -m kitty balances` |
| Who should pay whom | `python3 -m kitty settle` |
| One person's history | `python3 -m kitty history Bob` |
| Spending by category | `python3 -m kitty report` |
| Save a spreadsheet file | `python3 -m kitty export trip.csv` |

Amounts are positive numbers with at most two decimals. Dates are `YYYY-MM-DD`
(default: today). Names are not case-sensitive.
# Kitty Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** A `python3 -m kitty` command-line tool that tracks shared trip costs in `kitty.json` and prints JSON reports of balances, settlements, history and per-category spending.

**Architecture:** Pure functions over a plain `dict` state (`ledger.py` changes it, `reports.py` reads it). Exact money helpers live in `money.py`, and `store.py` loads and saves the file atomically. `cli.py` parses arguments, loads state, calls one function, prints JSON, and saves only if no `KittyError` was raised. Ledger functions take the raw strings from the command line and do all parsing and validation themselves.

**Tech Stack:** Python 3.9.6, standard library only (`argparse`, `decimal`, `json`, `csv`, `datetime`, `os`, `tempfile`, `re`), `unittest`.

**Spec:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-17-kitty-design.md`. Read it; it is the source of truth for every rule.

## Global Constraints

- Python 3.9.6 and standard library only. No `match`, no `X | Y` unions (use `Optional`). `list[str]`/`dict[str, str]` annotations are OK.
- Run as `python3 -m kitty <command>`. State is `kitty.json` in the current working directory.
- Success exits 0. Any refusal prints exactly one line `error: <message>` to stderr, nothing to stdout, exits 1, and leaves `kitty.json` byte-for-byte unchanged. Argparse usage errors count as refusals, so they also exit 1, not 2.
- JSON output is `json.dumps(obj, ensure_ascii=False)` on one line. Money is always a string with exactly two decimals.
- Money is `decimal.Decimal` throughout. Never use `float`.
- Run all tests from the project root: `python3 -m unittest discover tests -v`

## State schema (`kitty.json`, pinned so every task agrees)

```json
{"version": 1, "base_currency": "EUR", "members": ["Alice", "Bob"],
 "rates": {"USD": "0.92"}, "next_id": 2, "next_seq": 3,
 "expenses": [{"id": 1, "seq": 1, "date": "2026-07-14", "payer": "Alice",
   "description": "Dinner", "amount": "45.00", "currency": "USD", "rate": "0.92",
   "base_amount": "41.40", "category": "food",
   "shares": {"Alice": "20.70", "Bob": "20.70"}}],
 "payments": [{"seq": 2, "date": "2026-07-15", "from": "Bob", "to": "Alice",
   "amount": "20.70", "currency": "EUR", "rate": "1", "base_amount": "20.70"}]}
```

`seq` is one global counter across expenses and payments. It records the order things were added, which `history` uses to break ties. `shares` keys are kept in split order. Names are stored in the spelling they were first added with.

## Review Focus

1. **An amount or name that looks like an option** (`expense add Alice -5 Taxi`): refused with `error:` and exit 1, no traceback (Task 7 test `test_negative_amount_is_usage_error`).
2. **Accented names and case** (`José` added, then `JOSÉ` used): matched with `str.casefold()` and displayed as `José` (Task 3 test `test_accented_name_case_insensitive`).
3. **A damaged or hand-edited `kitty.json`** (invalid JSON, or valid JSON missing keys): refused with `error:`, no traceback (Task 2 test `test_load_corrupt`).
4. **Running in a folder with no kitty**: every command except `init` gives a clear error telling you to run `init` (Task 7 test `test_no_kitty_here`).
5. **Number look-alikes** (`1e3`, `nan`, `Infinity`, ` 45`, `4,50`, `+5`, `.5`): refused, never parsed by `Decimal` (Task 1 test `test_parse_amount_rejects`).

---

### Task 1: Project scaffold and money helpers

**Files:**
- Create: `.gitignore` (`kitty.json`, `__pycache__/`, `*.csv`), `kitty/__init__.py` (empty), `kitty/errors.py`, `kitty/money.py`
- Test: `tests/test_money.py`

**Interfaces:**
- Produces:
  - `kitty.errors.KittyError(Exception)`: a refusal; `str(e)` is the message.
  - `money.parse_amount(text: str) -> Decimal`: must fully match `^\d+(\.\d{1,2})?$` and be > 0, else `KittyError`. Returns the value quantized to `0.01`.
  - `money.parse_positive(text: str, what: str) -> Decimal`: must fully match `^\d+(\.\d+)?$` and be > 0. Used for rates, `--shares` and `--percent`. `what` names the thing in the error message.
  - `money.fmt(value: Decimal) -> str`: two decimals, half-up. `-0.00` prints as `"0.00"`.
  - `money.to_base(amount: Decimal, rate: Decimal) -> Decimal`: `(amount * rate)` quantized to `0.01` with `ROUND_HALF_UP`.
  - `money.split(total: Decimal, weights: list[Decimal]) -> list[Decimal]`
  - `money.parse_date(text: str) -> str`: must match `^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$` and be a real date (`datetime.strptime(text, "%Y-%m-%d")`). Returns `text`.
  - `money.parse_currency(text: str) -> str`: must match `^[A-Za-z]{3}$`. Returns it upper-cased.
  - Use `re.fullmatch` everywhere so a trailing newline can't slip through.

- [ ] **Step 1: Run `git init` in the project root, add `.gitignore`, and commit the existing `docs/` as the first commit.**

- [ ] **Step 2: Write failing tests in `tests/test_money.py`**

import datetime

import sys

import unittest

PROJECT_ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))


class CliBase(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self._tmp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.addCleanup(self._tmp.cleanup)
        self.tmpdir = self._tmp.name

    def run_cmd(self, *args):
        p = subprocess.run(
            [sys.executable, "-m", "kitty", *args], cwd=self.tmpdir,
            env={**os.environ, "PYTHONPATH": PROJECT_ROOT},
            capture_output=True, text=True)
        return p.returncode, p.stdout, p.stderr

    def setup_sam(self):
        for args in (["init", "EUR"], ["member", "add", "Alice"], ["member", "add", "Bob"],
                     ["rate", "set", "USD", "0.92"]):
            self.assertEqual(self.run_cmd(*args), (0, "", ""))
        self.assertEqual(self.run_cmd("expense", "add", "Alice", "45", "Dinner", "--currency",
                                      "USD", "--date", "2026-07-14", "--category", "food"),
                         (0, "1\n", ""))

    def state_bytes(self):
        with open(os.path.join(self.tmpdir, "kitty.json"), "rb") as f:
            return f.read()


class CliTest(CliBase):
    def test_sam_examples_end_to_end(self):
        self.setup_sam()
        expected = [
            (["member", "list"], '["Alice", "Bob"]'),
            (["expense", "list"], '[{"id": 1, "date": "2026-07-14", "payer": "Alice", "description": "Dinner", "amount": "45.00", "currency": "USD", "base_amount": "41.40", "category": "food", "shares": {"Alice": "20.70", "Bob": "20.70"}}]'),
            (["balances"], '{"Alice": "20.70", "Bob": "-20.70"}'),
            (["settle"], '[{"from": "Bob", "to": "Alice", "amount": "20.70"}]'),
            (["history", "Bob"], '[{"date": "2026-07-14", "description": "Dinner", "change": "-20.70", "balance": "-20.70"}]'),
            (["report"], '{"food": {"Alice": "20.70", "Bob": "20.70"}}'),
        ]
        for args, out in expected:
            self.assertEqual(self.run_cmd(*args), (0, out + "\n", ""), args)

    def test_multiword_description(self):
        self.run_cmd("init", "EUR")
        self.run_cmd("member", "add", "Alice")
        self.run_cmd("member", "add", "Bob")
        code, out, err = self.run_cmd("expense", "add", "Alice", "10", "Dinner", "at", "Luigi's",
                                      "--among", "Bob")
        self.assertEqual(code, 0, err)
        _, out, _ = self.run_cmd("expense", "list")
        self.assertEqual(json.loads(out)[0]["description"], "Dinner at Luigi's")

    def assert_refused(self, args):
        before = self.state_bytes()
        code, out, err = self.run_cmd(*args)
        self.assertEqual(code, 1, args)
        self.assertEqual(out, "", args)
        self.assertTrue(err.startswith("error: "), (args, err))
        self.assertEqual(len(err.splitlines()), 1, (args, err))
        self.assertNotIn("Traceback", err)
        self.assertEqual(self.state_bytes(), before, args)

    def test_refusals_leave_file_unchanged(self):
        self.setup_sam()
        cases = [
            "member add alice", "member remove Bob", "expense add Zed 5 X",
            "expense add Alice abc X", "expense add Alice 5 X --currency GBP",
            "expense add Alice 5 X --date 2026-02-30", "expense remove 99",
            "payment add Bob Bob 5", "rate set EUR 1", "history Zed", "init EUR",
            "bogus", "expense add Alice", "expense add Alice 5 X --cur USD",
            "", "member", "expense add Alice 1234567890123 X", "rate set USD 99999999999999",
        ]
        for c in cases:
            self.assert_refused(c.split())

    def test_negative_amount_is_usage_error(self):
        self.setup_sam()
        args = ["expense", "add", "Alice", "-5", "Taxi"]
        self.assert_refused(args)
        _, _, err = self.run_cmd(*args)
        self.assertIn("amount", err)
        self.assertNotIn("init", err)

    def test_no_kitty_here(self):
        code, out, err = self.run_cmd("balances")
        self.assertEqual(code, 1)
        self.assertIn("init", err)
        self.assertFalse(os.path.exists(os.path.join(self.tmpdir, "kitty.json")))

    def test_export_command(self):
        self.setup_sam()
        self.assertEqual(self.run_cmd("export", "out.csv"), (0, "", ""))
        with open(os.path.join(self.tmpdir, "out.csv"), newline="") as f:
            self.assertTrue(f.readline().strip())

    def test_default_date_is_today(self):
        self.run_cmd("init", "EUR")
        self.run_cmd("member", "add", "Alice")
        self.assertEqual(self.run_cmd("expense", "add", "Alice", "5", "Snack")[0], 0)
        _, out, _ = self.run_cmd("expense", "list")
        e = json.loads(out)[0]
        self.assertEqual(e["date"], datetime.date.today().isoformat())
        self.assertEqual(e["category"], "other")

    def test_empty_init_then_member_list(self):

        self.assertEqual(self.run_cmd("member", "list"), (0, "[]\n", ""))
import os
import tempfile

from kitty import store
from kitty.errors import KittyError


class StoreTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_init_and_load(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
            p = os.path.join(d, "kitty.json")
            store.init(p, "eur")
            s = store.load(p)
            self.assertEqual(s["base_currency"], "EUR")
            self.assertEqual(s["members"], [])
            self.assertEqual(s["next_id"], 1)

    def test_init_refuses_existing(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
            p = os.path.join(d, "kitty.json")
            store.init(p, "EUR")
            with open(p, "rb") as f:
                before = f.read()
            with self.assertRaises(KittyError):
                store.init(p, "EUR")
            with open(p, "rb") as f:
                self.assertEqual(f.read(), before)

    def test_load_missing(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
            with self.assertRaises(KittyError) as cm:
                store.load(os.path.join(d, "kitty.json"))
            self.assertIn("init", str(cm.exception))

    def test_load_corrupt(self):
        for content in ["{not json", "[]", '{"version": 1}']:
            with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
                p = os.path.join(d, "kitty.json")
                with open(p, "w") as f:
                    f.write(content)
                with self.assertRaises(KittyError):
                    store.load(p)

    def test_save_roundtrip_unicode(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
            p = os.path.join(d, "kitty.json")
            s = store.new_state("EUR")
            s["members"].append("José")
            store.save(p, s)
            self.assertEqual(store.load(p), s)
            self.assertEqual(os.listdir(d), ["kitty.json"])

## Review: kitty, branch `build`, c832567..a50abc9

**A note on the read-only rule first.** My first probe broke it. `mktemp -d` failed (the sandbox blocks the default temp dir), my `&&` chain stopped before the `cd`, and the kitty commands ran in the project folder. That created `/private/tmp/tmp12kvlzsp/pete/projects/kitty/kitty.json`, which had not existed before. I deleted that one file straight away. `git status --short --ignored` now shows only `.superpowers/`, HEAD is still `a50abc9` on `build`, and git tracked nothing because `kitty.json` is gitignored. All other probing ran in a temp dir under `$TMPDIR` (`/private/tmp/tmp12kvlzsp/tmp/`), which I have removed.

### Strengths
- The layout is clean: `money` holds pure helpers, `ledger` changes state, `reports` only reads it, `store` does atomic I/O and `cli` is thin. There are no import cycles.
- The money rules hold. Amounts round half-up into base (0.125 → 0.13). Splits round down and hand leftover cents out in listed order (10/3 gives 3.34, 3.33, 3.33; shares 1:2 gives 3.34, 6.66). `-0.00` is normalised. Balances always sum to zero.
- All of Sam's examples match byte-for-byte, including key order and `ensure_ascii=False`.
- Command-line usage errors exit 1 with one `error:` line, because `KittyParser.error` is inherited by the subparsers and `allow_abbrev=False` is set.
- Input parsing is strict and rejects look-alikes: `1e3`, Arabic digits, `.5`, `12.345`, `0.00`, `2026-02-29`, `2026-7-1`. It accepts `2024-02-29`.
- Settle tie-breaking is correct. I checked a case where alphabetical order and join order disagree (`Amy` is picked over `Zed`). History orders by date, then by the global sequence, across expenses and payments.
- `save` cleans up its temp file on any failure, including Ctrl-C. The 12-digit cap fixes the parked T1 traceback for normal inputs.
- 54 tests pass on Python 3.9.6. The CLI tests check exit code, empty stdout, one stderr line and unchanged file bytes.

### Issues

#### Critical (Must Fix)
1. **`export` can overwrite and destroy `kitty.json`** (`kitty/reports.py:85`, `export_csv`).
   - **What happens:** `python3 -m kitty export kitty.json` exits 0 and replaces the state file with CSV. Every later command then fails with "kitty.json is not valid JSON", so the whole trip's data is gone. Because macOS disks ignore case by default, `export KITTY.JSON` does the same; I reproduced both.
   - **Why it matters:** this breaks the spec's "Doesn't modify kitty.json" rule and the anti-goal of corrupting state. A non-programmer could easily type it.
   - **Fix:** refuse when the target is the state file, checking `os.path.exists(path) and os.path.samefile(path, STATE_FILE)`, or comparing `os.path.normcase(os.path.realpath(...))`. Also write the CSV to a temp file and `os.replace` it, so a failed export doesn't leave a half-written file. Add a CLI test for both spellings.

#### Important (Should Fix)
2. **Tracebacks from a hand-edited `kitty.json` that passes the key check, and bad files get saved** (`kitty/store.py:43-48`; no catch-all in `kitty/cli.py:127-133`).
   - **What happens:**
     - Tracebacks I reproduced: `"members": null` → TypeError; `"expenses": [{}]` → KeyError `'payer'`; a payer or share name not in `members` → KeyError; `"base_amount": "abc"` → `decimal.InvalidOperation`; `"shares": [...]` → AttributeError; `"next_id": "2"` → TypeError on `expense add`; `"rates": []` → TypeError on `rate set`.
     - Wrong output with exit 0: `"base_amount": NaN` (JSON allows NaN) prints `{"Alice": "NaN", ...}`. `"members": "Alice"` makes `member list` print `["A","l","i","c","e"]`. A share for an unknown name silently disappears from `report`.
     - Writes on top of corrupt data: `member add`, `rate set` and `expense add` succeed and rewrite the file. With malformed `shares`, `member remove Bob` succeeded even though Bob was referenced.
   - **Why it matters:** the spec says a corrupt file is refused with an error, not a traceback. Sam will be scripting against this file, so hand edits are realistic.
   - **Fix:** validate the whole structure in `store.load`, and refuse with `kitty.json is corrupt: <where>` on any failure:
     - `version == 1` and `base_currency` is a valid code.
     - `members` is a list of unique (casefold) non-empty strings.
     - `rates` is a dict of currency codes to positive decimal strings.
     - `next_id` and `next_seq` are ints (not bool).
     - Each expense and payment has every field, with the right types: money as two-decimal strings, valid dates, `shares` a dict, every name in `members`, IDs unique and below `next_id`, seqs below `next_seq`.
     - Load with `parse_constant` that rejects NaN and Infinity.

     As a safety net, also catch any other `Exception` in `main` and print a single `error: internal error: ...` line. Add tests that feed malformed records through the CLI.
   - **Plan issue:** the plan's Review Focus #3 only required checking top-level keys, which is why per-task reviews never caught this.
3. **Money precision runs out at the extremes the caps still allow** (`kitty/money.py:11, 36-46`).
   - **What happens:** rates can have 12+12 digits, so `amount × rate` can need about 38 significant digits. The default Decimal context keeps 28 digits and rounds first. I reproduced amount 999999999999.99 at rate 999999999999.999999999999 giving base_amount `999999999999989999999999.00`, where the exact value is `...999999.98999...`. So half-up rounding to the cent is broken, and sums of a few such values can drift.
   - **Why it matters:** this only bites at absurd values, but it is exactly the "drift by a cent" anti-goal, and the caps were meant to rule it out.
   - **Fix:** do the money math under `decimal.localcontext()` with `prec=60` or more, and set the `Inexact` trap if you want to be sure.

#### Minor (Nice to Have)
4. `kitty/ledger.py:156`: the ID regex lacks `re.ASCII`, so `expense remove ١` (an Arabic digit) removed expense 1. It also strips whitespace. This is the parked T4 item; add `re.ASCII` and drop the `.strip()`.
5. `kitty/money.py:11`: rates, `--shares` and `--percent` are capped at 12 decimals, but the spec says "any precision". `--percent A=33.3333333333333,...` is refused. Raise the fractional cap (the precision fix in #3 makes that safe), or note the deviation in the README.
6. A very small rate produces a 0.00 base amount. At rate 1e-12, `expense add Bob 0.01 ... --currency USD` and a 5 USD payment both store base `0.00` and exit 0. Consider refusing when the base amount rounds to 0.00.
7. `kitty/store.py:58` (`save`): `NamedTemporaryFile` creates the file with 0600 permissions, so `kitty.json` loses its original permissions after every save. There is also no `fsync` before `os.replace`. Fix with `os.chmod` (copy the existing file's mode, or 0644) and `f.flush(); os.fsync()`.
8. `kitty/cli.py`: giving an option twice (`--among Bob --among Cara`) silently keeps the last one. Options in the middle of the description (`45 Lunch --category food at place`) are refused with "unrecognized arguments". The spec only promises before or after, so that's acceptable, but worth a line in the README.
9. `kitty/cli.py:88-120`: the `print_after` flow is fragile (a T7 deferred item). The variable only exists on one branch. Set `print_after = None` up front.
10. `kitty/reports.py:91`: CSV fields starting with `=`, `+`, `-` or `@` will run as formulas when Sam opens the export in a spreadsheet. Low risk, since it's his own data.
11. Test gaps:
    - The settle tie test (`tests/test_reports_balances.py:39`) doesn't separate alphabetical order from join order.
    - The zero-share history test (`tests/test_reports_more.py:51`) is weak.
    - Split order isn't asserted for `--exact`, `--shares` or `--percent`.
    - There is no test for a successful foreign-currency payment.
    - There is no test for save-failure cleanup.
    - Two CLI tests don't check setup exit codes.
    - There are no tests for corrupt records or for exporting onto the state file.

### Triage of ledger deferred/parked items
| Item | Fix before merge? |
|---|---|
| T1: huge numbers cause `InvalidOperation` traceback | Fixed by the cap for normal input. Yes for the leftover precision problem (#3), fixed together with #5. |
| T2: no save-failure cleanup test | No, but cheap to add. |
| T2: kitty.json gets 0600 permissions | No (Minor #7). |
| T4: ID regex lacks `re.ASCII` and strips whitespace | Yes. It's a one-liner and I reproduced the wrong-expense removal. |
| T4: split order not asserted for exact/shares/percent | No, but add with the fix wave. |
| T4: no foreign-currency payment success test | No, but add. |
| T5: settle tie test doesn't separate alphabetical from join order | No (behaviour verified correct by probe); add the variant. |
| T6: weak zero-share history assertion | No. |
| T7: fragile `print_after` flow | No, but trivial. |
| T7: setup exit codes unchecked in two CLI tests | No. |
| T7: export test doesn't compare the header | No. The header is checked in `test_reports_more.py:76`. |
| T7: duplicated manual-check test | No. |

### Declined to judge
- Names starting with `-` inside `--among`/`--exact`, e.g. `--among -dash`: argparse treats them as flags, and `--among=-dash` works. It's general argparse behaviour, the error is clean, and the spec doesn't cover it.
- Ctrl-C tracebacks outside `save`: not "bad input", and a Ctrl-C inside `save` already leaves the file intact.
- BrokenPipe or stdout write failures (e.g. piping to `head`): an environment issue the spec doesn't cover, and I couldn't trigger it with outputs this small.
- A race between `init`'s exists-check and `os.replace`: single-user local tool, so the risk is negligible.
- `casefold` vs `lower` for names and categories: both meet "case-insensitive", and casefold is the better choice.
- Sorting non-ASCII category names by code point: the spec says "alphabetical" without a locale, so code point is reasonable.
- Description words with newlines in CSV: the `csv` module quotes them correctly.

### Recommendations
- Make `store.load` a real validator, the single gate for whether a state file is trustworthy, and test it with a table of malformed records run through the CLI.
- Put a high-precision Decimal context around all money math.
- Guard `export` against the state file and make the export write atomic.
- Then do one small fix wave for #4, #7 and #9 plus the listed tests.

### Assessment
**Ready to merge?** With fixes

**Reasoning:** The core money logic, Sam's JSON formats and handling of normal bad input are solid and well tested. But `export kitty.json` silently destroys all trip data, and a hand-edited file that keeps the top-level keys still causes tracebacks and writes over bad data. Both break explicit spec guarantees and must be fixed before merge, ideally with the precision fix (#3).
